Blair.note: Thrown early, with the double down.

Casey.note: Thrown early, with the double down.

Drew.note: Ellis winked, so Casey only has Finley's 3; I'm at 7. Likely lose, but throwing at Casey (likely cat) returns my card.

Ellis.note: Thrown early, with the double down.

Finley.note: Thrown early, with the double down.

Alex.confusing: The rules say at most 2 Meowfia, yet rounds 2 and 3 each had three cats (Alex, Blair, Ellis, then Alex, Blair, Casey). So Finley's 'three cats on Drew' report was true, and I helped get Finley eggsecuted by calling it impossible. It was also unclear that special actions like double down only happen if you win the floor.
Alex.fun: Round 3, when Ellis suddenly collapsed from a Wink. That wiped out Ellis's 6 votes on Casey and swung the eggsecution to Drew, just as I called the third CAW CAW.
Alex.change: Either enforce the 2-Meowfia cap or state clearly that it can be broken. Players reason from that rule, and it decided round 2. I'd also let a declared special action go through even when the player doesn't win the floor.
Alex.regret: I'd take back the round 1 Maine Coon challenge that bet my whole nest. Ellis's Pigeon claim was a lie (Ellis was the Mouser). I should have kept my cards and thrown a few low ones at Blair, which would have earned the consolation card back and kept me in the race.

Blair.confusing: The rules say at most 2 Meowfia per round, yet rounds 2 and 3 each had three, so Finley's 'three cats on Drew' report was true, while the stated rules made it look impossible. The Maine Coon was also in the pool but never described, so I only learned what it does when Alex used its challenge.
Blair.fun: Winking Ellis in round 3 to wipe out the 6 votes on my fellow cat Casey. That flipped a likely loss into Drew's eggsecution.
Blair.change: Make sure the setup follows the stated Meowfia cap, or drop the cap from the rules, and give every animal in the pool a description. Players can only reason well if the rules match what the game actually does.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I should have winked Ellis as soon as Ellis doubled down on Casey, instead of my first wink attempt going nowhere because I didn't get the floor. It worked out, but it was nearly too late.

Casey.confusing: The rules said at most 2 Meowfia per round, but rounds 2 and 3 each had 3 (Alex, Blair, Ellis, then Alex, Blair, me). So Finley's three-cat Owl report was true, yet everyone, me included, treated it as impossible. The Maine Coon was also in the pool, but its ability was never described.
Casey.fun: My favourite moment was round 3. My Sphinx visit found that Drew was the Kookaburra, and I doubled down on him. When the table turned on me, I bonded with Alex and the votes swung back to Drew, which turned a lost position into a doubled win.
Casey.change: Either enforce the stated limit on Meowfia per round or correct the rules text, and describe every animal in the pool, including the Maine Coon. Right now players reasoning correctly from the rules get punished.
Casey.regret: In round 2, I should have backed Finley's report outright and pressed Alex's unverifiable Turkey claim and Blair's late claim. That might have broken the 8–8 tie, which went to Meowfia and got Farm Finley eggsecuted.

Drew.confusing: The rules say at most 2 Meowfia per round, but rounds 2 and 3 each had three cats. That made Finley's true three-cat Owl report look impossible, and I gave ground on it.
Drew.fun: Round 1, when Alex's failed Maine Coon challenge outed him, and I got to throw my whole nest, including the King, for a clean 40 points.
Drew.change: The alignment cap should match what actually happens. If three cats can show up, the rules should say so, because players use the cap to catch lies.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I should have called CAW CAW right after Ellis did instead of asking more questions. With Ellis still alive, his 6 votes would have got Casey eggsecuted before the handshakes and the wink turned it around.

Ellis.confusing: The rules said at most 2 Meowfia per round, but rounds 2 and 3 each had 3. In round 2 I argued Finley's three-cat report was impossible, and it turned out to be true. A hard limit that isn't enforced makes rules-based deduction misleading.
Ellis.fun: In round 3 my Owl result (only a Kookaburra visited Blair) quietly confirmed Drew's claim, and it felt great to put everything on Casey on a correct read.
Ellis.change: Either enforce the Meowfia cap or state clearly that it can be exceeded. Also, a dead player's thrown cards still leave their nest but count for nothing, which makes the wink feel very swingy.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I revealed my strong Owl info loudly and doubled down early, which made me the obvious wink target. My 6 cards then counted as no votes, so Drew got 7 votes against Casey's 4 instead of Casey getting 10. I should have kept a lower profile until close to CAW, or let Drew carry the argument.

Finley.confusing: The rules said at most 2 Meowfia, but rounds 2 and 3 each had three. The Maine Coon was also missing from the animal rules. Because of that, my true Owl report of three cats on Drew sounded impossible and got me killed.
Finley.fun: Catching Ellis's Hawk claim with my Owl report in round 2. It was a clean, fact-based catch, even though the table didn't believe me.
Finley.change: Make the rules match the real setup, either by enforcing the 2-Meowfia cap or by stating the real cap. Also list every animal in the pool, like the Maine Coon, in the animal rules.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I only pushed on Ellis. I should have pointed out that Blair's and Alex's claims didn't fit my three-cat report either, since both of them later voted me out. Then I would have thrown just the low cards and kept the 12s back, because that day was a tossup.

review.title: The Third Cat
review.headline: A truthful Owl got eggsecuted because the game secretly dealt three cats.
review.summary: In round 1, Alex's fake Tit claim ran into the real Tit, Blair. Alex then outed himself as Maine Coon with a failed challenge, and Farm won easily. In rounds 2 and 3 the setup broke its own rule and dealt three Meowfia. In round 2, Finley's accurate Owl report showed three cats visiting Drew. The cats called it impossible under the rules, and the table eggsecuted Finley, who was telling the truth. In round 3, Blair's anonymous Wink killed Ellis and wiped out Ellis's six doubled-down votes. That flipped the eggsecution onto Drew, and Blair won the game 84 to 69.

rounds.recap: Alex claimed Tit, and Blair, the real Tit, answered by doubling down five cards on Alex. Finley doubled down on Alex too. Facing 8 votes, Alex made a Maine Coon challenge. It failed because Ellis's Pigeon claim was false, and it confirmed Alex as a cat. Everyone except Ellis threw at Alex, and Farm won.

Finley's Owl report on Drew named Floofer, Maine Coon and Mouser, which was true: Alex, Blair and Ellis were all cats. Ellis and Alex said three cats was impossible under the rules. Farm still piled onto Ellis. But the three cats' 10 votes on Finley beat the 8 Farm votes on Ellis, so the truthful Owl was eggsecuted.

Casey (Sphinx) found the Kookaburra and doubled down on Drew, using Drew's confusion-caused -2 as the case against him. Blair joined in. Ellis's Owl report confirmed Drew, and Ellis and Finley doubled down on Casey for 9 votes. Then Blair winked Ellis, which cancelled 6 of those votes. Drew went 7 to 4, and the three cats won.

highlights.text: Blair answered Alex's fake Tit claim at once by doubling down the whole nest: 'There's only one Tit. You're lying.'
Facing 8 votes, Alex bet everything on a Maine Coon challenge, missed one guess, and revealed himself as a cat.
Finley's honest Owl report named three cats, and the cats got it dismissed by quoting the 'at most 2 Meowfia' rule, which the game had broken.
With 9 votes on Casey, Blair's anonymous Wink killed Ellis, cancelled six doubled-down votes, and sent the vote to Drew.

confusions.what: Said Alex claimed Tit only after Blair did. Alex actually claimed Tit first.
Used a Maine Coon challenge, a card the rules sheet never describes. Players had to guess how it works and what it costs.
Tried to explain the three-cat Owl report as 'maybe a Maine Coon swap'. Nobody knew what Maine Coon does, so the true explanation (a setup bug) was out of reach.
Called Finley's report impossible because at most 2 players are Meowfia. That was correct by the written rules, but the engine had dealt 3 cats, so the rules misled the whole table.
Said 'three cats can't exist' while being the third cat himself. The rules text and the real deal disagreed.
The log says 'Drew (Falcon) is hugged: no effect at tier 60', but Drew was the Owl in round 1, and the hug happened in round 2. A debug or engine line leaked into the record.

worked: Crimson Kunzea double down: early public bets created clear commitments. Blair's instant double down on the Tit clash and the 9-vs-5 standoff in round 3 were the best moments of the game.
Unique Farm roles (Tit): 'each animal goes to only one player' made a role clash a real, checkable contradiction, and round 1 was decided fairly on it.
Owl report listing animals: twice it gave hard evidence (catching the fake Hawk, confirming Drew's Kookaburra) and pushed players to confront each other.
Anonymous Mouser Wink: held through two rounds, then used at the perfect moment. It was a dramatic reversal, and nobody could tell who did it.
problems: Setup bug: rounds 2 and 3 each dealt 3 Meowfia (Alex, Blair, Ellis; then Alex, Blair, Casey), breaking the 'at most 2' rule. It decided round 2, because true information was rejected as impossible. Enforce the cap in the engine.

Maine Coon is in the pool but missing from the rules text. Alex was Maine Coon all three rounds, and a challenge that fails publicly reveals the challenger as a cat. Document the card, and consider keeping a failed challenge secret. Also check role assignment for randomness: Alex was Maine Coon three times, Ellis Mouser twice and Casey Kookaburra twice.

Golden Wattle pays a Meowfia +3 no matter who they bond with. Cats offered handshakes to everyone, and Farm quickly learned that an offer is a tell (Blair, Finley). Make it a risk for cats too, for example -3 to a Meowfia who bonds with Farm when Farm wins the round.

Wink plus Crimson Kunzea: a player who doubled down has committed their votes publicly, so a single Wink can erase them all (Ellis's 6). One action swung the game. Consider letting committed double-down votes count even if the thrower dies afterwards.

Kookaburra confusion makes the player really discard cards (Drew fell to 1 card), and the fake loss became the cats' main argument against him. Consider making confused counts informational only, with no real draw or discard. Also remove the leaked 'tier 60' engine text from logs.
